QF.id: Cat III AIF Fees and Performance_68

question.text: An AIF follows an 'absolute return' strategy. The appropriate benchmark is:

answer.text: A fixed pre-determined rate (e.g., 10% p.a.) set at launch

explanation.text: The Logic: Per page 227 of the workbook, absolute-return strategies are not benchmarked against a broad-based market index or a relative benchmark; instead the benchmark may be a fixed rate predetermined by the Investment Manager at launch, such as 10% per annum. The Trap: Market indices apply to relative/directional strategies and the Sharpe Ratio is a risk-adjusted performance metric, not a benchmark. Note: The investment strategy (including its benchmarking approach) is defined in the fund's PPM.
